findings: The predecessor was preserved: the frozen BACKLOG-FLEET-SEEDED-STABILITY-02 receipt and HOLD review still hash to efbd36ba4d8178dcddf9554953d553d2aea6168c04bad11b2f6d9ccff29d5311 and be288bc446d1a047b794512c3a9ae471213a8e9a51f0a5c48ca43b2982af6b70. R3 adds a fresh run and does not rewrite R2.

Independent raw recomputation found exactly 288 unique model-repeat-suite-case cells, 96 complete triplets and 192 repeat-zero comparisons. All 288 responses are HTTP 200/error-free; their semantic projections, semantic SHA-256 values and descriptive scores recompute exactly, and all 192 seeded comparisons are exact. All 288 response IDs are unique and all 192 baseline-repeat pairs have distinct IDs, creation metadata and timings, so duplicated response rows do not explain the observed stability.

BLOCKING request-binding false positive: every stored request object reconstructs exactly from the frozen panel and has temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, seed 20260826, streaming disabled and prompt caching disabled, but zero of 288 request_sha256 values equals the canonical SHA-256 of the request stored on the same row. The 288 stored hashes instead equal the first 288 entries of the real 292-call HTTP sequence: four route canaries plus 288 experimental requests. Canary hashes occur at sample indices 0, 73, 146 and 219, and hashes for the final four qwen36-moe requests are left pending. The generic chat-completion hook enqueues route canaries, while the inherited R2 provenance finalizer later overwrites each captured request with a reconstructed request without updating its SHA. Consequently request_retention reports 288 although no row retains a cryptographically self-consistent per-sample HTTP argument, and the frozen request-at-send-time contract is not independently verified.

BLOCKING binary-identity false positive: the raw snapshots bind four healthy aliases to distinct positive backend PIDs, /proc command lines, executable paths and GGUF paths. All four GGUF SHA-256/byte values match the frozen registry, and an independent live rehash reproduced the four recorded GGUF digests and sizes. Both executable files also independently rehash to their recorded values. However, the frozen registry contains only runtime.binary paths, not expected executable SHA-256 or byte values. The implementation names its gate physical_binary_hash_match_rate but computes it solely from binary_hash_present, accepting any 64-character value. The preregistration explicitly requires executable SHA-256 equality to the frozen registry and aborts on mismatch, so this gate cannot establish the registered condition.

The physical snapshots were added before each route's first experimental request by the frozen call order and are provenance inputs. The runner state and physical identity hashes match their receipt ledger entries; MainPID 145666 and NRestarts 0 are preserved, the initial qwen38 route is restored healthy and embedding returns HTTP 200. Receipt SHA-256 fcb390b241a9d8b369e58c08d938e03782e71ed6c99efeaecffe1ec14b404e7c, fingerprint 64eea58e2abb83963a986be0a3add6092fecbb133aab362c82f3558e3e7efd5b, all 23 provenance input records, both implementation hashes and implementation digest badb1e7f1513c914a556e0ff1b596fc5a17ff118314aed9e3595b80f4d94da04 recompute exactly. The terminal completed state is bound before receipt creation.

The narrow descriptive observation is 192/192 exact semantic repeat comparisons for 288 distinct live responses under the reconstructed frozen seeded contract. It does not establish quality superiority, unseeded determinism or generalization: 126 of 192 math responses end at the token cap, including nine descriptively scored passes, so deterministic truncation is compatible with perfect stability. Neither allowed physically-bound R3 claim may be approved while the two binding gates above are false positives.

Minimum proportional successor fix: isolate sample HTTP capture from switch canaries, bind request and response atomically per call, assert a zero pending queue and per-row request hash equality before receipt, and prevent the R2 reconstruction pass from overwriting captured requests. Freeze expected executable SHA-256/bytes in a versioned registry input and compare equality rather than digest presence. Preserve this packet unchanged and rerun under a new task/version.
